key_insight: As the interfacial Atwood number increases, multi-layer Rayleigh-Taylor instability starts earlier, mixes faster, and evolves from two weakly coupled interfaces into one strongly coupled turbulent region.
engineering_relevance: This matters for predicting mixing, buoyancy-driven transport, and interface breakup in layered fluids, stratified flows, and energy/material processing systems.
method: 3D fully compressible direct numerical simulations (DNS) of a three-layer Rayleigh-Taylor configuration
Ten cases spanning a broad range of interfacial At to isolate stratification effects
Tracked vorticity, mixing-layer growth, density fluctuations, TKE, and energy partitioning
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a consistent progression through onset, quasi-exponential growth, and nonlinear saturation across cases, with stronger stratification producing earlier vorticity growth, faster mixing-layer expansion, and late-time spectra near -11/5 scaling.
watch_item: Results come from idealized DNS and may not transfer directly to high-Re, finite-domain, or experimentally noisy systems without careful validation.
paper_title: Direct numerical simulations of multi-layer Rayleigh-Taylor instability under asymmetric interfacial density stratification
